entries.target_post_text: Your First AI Music Video: What I Learned Making Four in Eighteen Days — Queso 3:49 / 93 shots, READ ME 2:49 / 66 shots, Juego 2:28 / 35 shots
entries.own_post_text:
93 shots for a 3:49 cut. That single number is the whole story.
Generation stopped being the constraint a while ago. What ate the 18 days was deciding which of those shots was good enough — and binning the ones that almost were.
Near-misses are the expensive part. A shot that's 90% right still has to go, and making that call takes longer than throwing out something obviously broken would have.
The mistakes that cost you money were selection mistakes, not generation mistakes.

entries.target_post_text: Syntax was always going to expire. What holds its value is knowing what breaks in production and when a simple change isn't simple. (转自 @housecor 25 年 web dev 知识盘点, 149 likes)
entries.own_post_text:
Agreed on the first half, less sure on the second.
"Knowing what breaks" is knowledge about one specific system at one specific moment. It decays fast, because the system keeps moving under you.
I maintain a client template set — about 30 of them. Last quarter I changed something 80-odd times, and a good chunk of what I "knew" about how it breaks went stale each time.
So the part that actually survived wasn't the map. It was how fast I notice when the map's wrong.
Which is probably why I care more about being woken up at 3am than about never being woken up.

entries.target_post_text: We've had 47 calls with private equity teams since May... ONE - People are the bottleneck (16/47). TWO - Teams are too big, but nobody wants to cut without proof. THREE - What happens to the freed-up capacity is still an open question.
entries.own_post_text:
Useful data. One pushback from the other side of the table.
The PE framing is "fewer people, or more output from the same people". Inside a company nobody frames it that way. The question is "can I put this in front of the board next quarter with enough evidence it won't blow up".
Different problems. PE wants a productivity number. We need a defensible one.
A team can show 40% faster throughput on one workflow and still get told no, because the number won't survive contact with finance. The gain is real and it isn't bankable.
None of the 47 calls seemed to ask which of those two they're solving.

entries.target_post_text: We spent a year running a GTM agency for cyber and devtools companies... The work was fine. The handover was missing. Failed AI projects usually aren't bad builds. They're orphaned builds.
entries.own_post_text:
Orphaned builds is the right frame. One addition.
The thing that gets orphaned usually isn't the number. It's the definition sitting behind the number.
I can hand someone a dashboard. Handing them what "转化" means that week is the part that dies, because it was never written anywhere — it just lived in the head of the person who set it.
Your day-one exit criteria are right. I'd add one: for every metric in the handover, can you write the sentence you'd use to settle an argument about it? If not, you're handing over a number without a meaning.
Which runbooks exists is the easy question. Which assumptions were never written down is the expensive one.

entries.target_post_text: Eva's feedback in plain English — 8 点诚实技术评测. 2/ 最好的部分是它能说我不知道 3/ 一条claim没扛住: 改口后旧事实仍排在前面 4-7/ 希望agent能自己纠错 / 别用少量样本自我调参 / 记忆变多后要重测那条我不知道的线 / 不该永久删除
entries.own_post_text:
Point 3 is the real one. Fading the old fact but still returning it, old answer first — that's not a ranking bug. It's the system telling you it has no concept of superseded.
My rule after getting this wrong repeatedly: never store a generalized fact. Store the specific failure instead.
"User prefers dark mode" has no expiry. You can't tell when it stops being true.
"The user complained on 2024-03 that the export dropped a column, and it dropped it again after the refactor" never expires, because it's not a claim about the world. It's a scar.
Generalizations are exactly why old facts are unretirable. You can't tell whether a vague claim is still true, so all you can do is demote it.
Point 7 is right for the same reason — deletion is scary mostly because people stored things that were never worth keeping.

Frank 的论点: **泛化事实没有过期时间, 因为你无法判断一条模糊的claim什么时候不再为真, 所以只能降权、永远无法退休. 具体失败有疤, 疤不会过期.** 顺带用 point 7(不该永久删除)做闭环: 大家怕删除, 主要是因为他们存了一堆本来就不该存的东西. 选目标理由: 本轮已验证'技术/实操向受众反应更好'(见下方finding), 故不选资本/买方类帖.
